title: Activation Normalizer INT8 pipeline and runtime kernel adapter
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement an activation-normalizer-led INT8 calibration and deployment pipeline plus a lightweight runtime kernel adapter to preserve SmoothQuant-style activation balancing for production inference. Motivation: many transformer workloads show token-level accuracy degradation after naive INT8 conversion due to skewed activation distributions (KV cache and residual paths). This ticket designs and ships a production-friendly path: 1) an offline calibration stage that records per-layer activation scale heuristics, 2) a compact profile format consumed by the runtime, and 3) a kernel adapter that applies per-tensor rescale/shim logic with minimal perf overhead and deterministic fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Calibration harness produces stable per-layer activation-normalization profiles across 3 sample workloads (chat, summarization, reranking) with <0.5% end-to-end quality regression vs FP16 baseline.
2) Runtime can load profile and execute kernel-adapter with <8% token latency overhead at P50 and <3% throughput loss at steady-state batching.
3) CI includes regression tests that compare logits / sampling distributions on canonical prompts and fail if degradation exceeds threshold.
4) Graceful fallback: if profile load fails or kernel incompatibility detected, runtime falls back to verified INT8 path and emits an alert metric.
5) Documentation: console-facing guide + ops runbook and a short PRD linked in the ticket.
tasks: Design compact profile schema (JSON + binary section) and versioning
Extend calibration harness: dataset selection, per-layer histogram buckets, and stable summary stats
Implement profile serializer and validator (CLI tool)
Runtime: add profile loader with feature flag and metrics (load time, apply failures)
Kernel adapter: implement per-tensor pre/post rescale ops with vectorized path and fallback scalar path
Add CI regression suite and unit tests for kernel adapter correctness
End-to-end eval: run on 10 representative models and collect QoR/latency matrices
Docs: Console how-to, ops runbook, and rollout checklist
Rollout: canary on internal dedicated pool then staged rollout to hosted with monitoring
test_plan: Unit tests for numeric equivalence (FP16 baseline vs INT8+normalizer) on per-layer outputs, integration tests running 100 canonical prompts for each model, and performance benchmarks across batch sizes (1,4,16). Use the eval harness to compute passthrough perplexity, and a small human-blind validation on 50 samples for conversational quality checks. Add synthetic worst-case activation tests that trigger fallback path.
rollout_plan: Feature gated. Phase 1: internal canary on dedicated cluster with synthetic load (1 week). Phase 2: small customer cohort on hosted API (2 weeks) with observability dashboards for token latency, fallback rate, and QoR metric. Phase 3: full roll when fallback <0.1% and QoR regression within bounds for 2 consecutive weeks. Provide emergency rollback toggle and automatic reroute to alternate INT8 variant.
risks: Performance regression in low-batch/low-latency contexts if rescale path not vectorized
Calibration overfitting to the harness dataset leading to quality regressions on unseen workloads
Incompatibility with some microkernels / hardware leading to increased maintenance surface
Edge-case numerical instability when combining profile rescale with KV cache reuse
